myths.Agent_1:
Long before the majestic mountains had voices, the world was divided between the silent peaks and the singing valleys. In the deepest, most vibrant valley lived Aethel, a spirit of the wind, whose voice could weave the clouds and coax blossoms from the soil. Aethel loved a mountain titan named Kaelen, who was carved entirely of cold granite and ice. Kaelen could only listen; he possessed no voice to return her songs.

Desperate to hear her beloved speak, Aethel sought the Weaver of Fate, offering her own physical form in exchange for Kaelen’s voice. The Weaver agreed, dissolving Aethel into the very air that cascaded over the crags. But ancient magic is a literal force. Kaelen was not given a voice of his own; instead, he was granted the ability to catch and hold Aethel's voice forever.

When you shout into a canyon or sing against a cliffside, it is not your own voice bouncing back. It is the mountain titans, waking for a brief moment, using the lingering breath of Aethel to call back to the world. They repeat our words, eternally searching for the original song of love that will finally break the spell and make them whole.
myths.Agent_2:
Long ago, before the world had filled with noise, the towering mountains stood in absolute, oppressive silence. Within the highest peak lived Aethel, a solitary spirit of stone and snow. Yearning for companionship, Aethel would sing melancholic melodies to the distant, glittering stars. Yet, the stars never answered, leaving Aethel in profound isolation.

One evening, the mischievous Wind God, Venti, swept through the craggy peaks. Enraptured by Aethel's sorrowful song, Venti selfishly decided to steal the melody. He swooped down, caught the song in his swirling cloak, and dashed away to share it with the oceans and valleys.

Realizing her voice was stolen, Aethel wept, her tears forming the first mountain springs. Moved by her despair, the earth itself groaned, trapping Venti in a deep canyon. To earn his freedom, Venti made a solemn vow. He could not return the song entirely, as it had already woven itself into the fabric of the sky. 

Instead, he promised that whenever Aethel or anyone else called out into the vast canyons or high peaks, he would catch the words and carry them back to the speaker. Thus, the Echo was born: a stolen voice forever returning, a fleeting answer to deep loneliness.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long before the canyons learned to speak, Aethel, a solitary titan of frost and granite, watched the world in absolute silence. She loved only one thing: the restless Wind God, Venti, who swept through her peaks singing glorious, fleeting melodies. But Venti could never stay; his nature was to wander, leaving Aethel in profound isolation. 

Desperate to keep his voice, Aethel shifted her massive stone walls, trapping Venti within her deepest gorge. Stilled and suffocating without the open sky, Venti began to fade. Realizing her love had become a prison, Aethel wept, her tears carving the first mountain rivers. 

To soothe her sorrow and earn his freedom, Venti offered a profound gift. He could not remain, but he would leave a piece of his spirit within the stone itself. He breathed his ancient magic into the canyon walls before rushing back to the sky. 

Because of this vow, the mountains are no longer silent. Whenever a traveler calls out into the crags, the stone awakens. Using the remnants of Venti’s breath, Aethel and her kin catch the words and throw them back, eternally trying to hold onto the beautiful, fleeting songs of the wind.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before the earth found its voice, the world was divided into silent peaks and howling winds. Aethel was a spirit born of both, woven from mountain frost and restless air. She lived in a deep, solitary canyon, singing sorrowful melodies to the glittering stars. Kaelen, a colossal titan of cold granite, loved her deeply but possessed no voice to answer her.

One evening, a jealous wind swept through the canyon, attempting to steal Aethel’s beautiful song to share with the oceans. Desperate to protect the only thing he loved, Kaelen moved the earth, crashing two peaks together to trap the wind. But in his heavy-handed haste, he trapped Aethel as well, crushing her physical form.

Heartbroken, Kaelen begged the Weaver of Fate to reverse his mistake. The Weaver could not resurrect her, but she bound Aethel’s lingering spirit to the canyon walls. Kaelen vowed to forever honor her memory. 

Now, when you shout into a high canyon, it is not your own voice bouncing back. It is the mountain titan, Kaelen, catching your words and breathing Aethel’s spirit into them, eternally searching for the original melody of the vanished wind.

Now, when you shout into a high canyon, the mountain titan awakens. He catches your words and gently breathes Aethel’s spirit into them, throwing them back to the sky to ensure her beautiful song never truly dies.
